l4Discriminating.text: Environmental conditions became unstable or oscillatory after day 27 (thermostat malfunction, HVAC control loop hunting, or seasonal microclimate transition), causing episodic high-variance behavior; underlying measurement systems remain stable and drift is environmental, not instrumental. — Day 40 persistence of high-variance episodes is consistent with an ongoing environmental oscillation rather than a one-time disturbance. However, the hypothesis predicts that facility environmental logs (thermostat settings, HVAC maintenance records, or seasonal transition notes) should document the transition after day 27. No such documentation is noted in your meticulous records. If a thermostat malfunction or control-loop hunting were occurring, facility staff would have reported abnormal temperature or humidity swings, or you would have initiated manual monitoring. The absence of such documentation is a strong negative signal. Additionally, the precisely 3-day spacing of peaks (days 28, 31, 34, 40) is more consistent with a periodic external schedule than with an uncontrolled environmental oscillation, which would show irregular or phase-drifting peaks. Downgraded from 0.18 because Day 40 continues the episodic pattern, but the lack of facility documentation now weighs more heavily against environmental malfunction.
